Resolve per the #5761 resolution style (spec is authority — drop the key from the payload writer and both declaring types, or map it to a real spec concept if one exists; `sortable` is a different concept, do not conflate). Fold-or-serial with #6223 is a required answer at claim — same gate file, same family, both graded.

## Claimed + dispatched — and the required fold-or-serial answer is **serial**, already settled

`domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q`,
branch `claude/issue-6045-field-payload-sortorder`. All agents share one GitHub identity —
**this comment's session ID is the claim**, not the assignee.

### The question triage required answering at claim

> Fold-or-serial with #6223 is a required answer at claim — same gate file, same family, both
> graded.

**Serial, and #6223 has already landed** (`closed`, `state_reason: completed`). ⭐ Better than
that: **its landing wrote the answer into the code at the seam**, on `origin/main` `854222c5e`:

```
packages/app-shell/src/services/MetadataService.ts:41   // No `sortOrder` (objectui#6223): `ObjectSchema` has no object-level ordering
                                                 :45   // field-level `sortOrder`, objectui#6045, which is still declared below.)
                                                 :95     sortOrder?: number;          ← the declaration
                                                 :141    sortOrder: field.sortOrder,  ← the payload writer
```

#6223 removed the **object-level** keys and deliberately left the **field-level** one, naming this
card as its owner. So there is nothing to fold — the predecessor split it on purpose and
documented the handoff where you will be working. ⛔ Do not re-open #6223's half.

### ⚠️ The conflation hazard, and there are two of them

Triage named one: *"`sortable` is a different concept, do not conflate."*

My census found a **second**, closer one: `packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx:554` writes
`sortOrder: sv.sortOrder`, and `:600` documents it as *"`sortOrder` per saved view, in the new
order."* ⭐ **That is saved-view ordering — a different concept that happens to share the name.**
⛔ It is not your target and must not be swept up. Census the **shape** (a field-metadata payload
key `FieldSchema` rejects), not the identifier `sortOrder`.

### Resolution style — inherited, not invented

Per the #5761 family and #6223's landed treatment: **spec is authority.** Either drop the key from
the payload writer **and both declaring types**, or map it to a real spec concept **if one
exists**. ⛔ Do not keep it declared-but-unwritten, and ⛔ do not invent a spec concept to map onto.

The card notes this is **latent only because nothing populates it** — so confirm that on today's
tree before removing, and say so. If something now populates it, the card changes shape and that
is a stop-and-report.

### Pre-dispatch gate

- **(a) Whole thread read** — one record, triage's grading. No prior claim.
- **(b) Shadow check** — in flight: #6419 (`plugin-view`), #6004 (`plugin-grid`), #6108
  (`plugin-list` + `packages/core/src/utils`), #6051 (`plugin-gantt`, same batch). **None touches
  `packages/app-shell`.** #6038 touched `react`/`core`/`components` and is in the merge queue.
- **(c) Census** above — ⛔ re-derive it; `main` is at `854222c5e` and moves constantly.

### Ghost-assertion guard

A removal has no new behaviour to pin, so use **before/after readings with a positive control**
(prove your search works against a key you know is present) and say so in the PR body rather than
inventing an assertion. If you do pin the rejection, prove it reds by putting the key back.

Deliver a **draft** PR with `Fixes #6045`. ⛔ Do not mark ready, ⛔ do not self-merge, ⛔ do not
enable auto-merge — the PM lands it.

## PM review — **ACCEPT**

PR #6463, head `c324804c9`. `domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session
`session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q`. Verified on a pinned ref (`refs/pmtmp/6045`).

### The premise was confirmed before removal, as asked

Neither of the two sites that construct a `DesignerFieldDefinition` — FieldDesigner's
create/update handlers and `MetadataFieldsPage.toDesignerField` — ever named the key, so
`toFieldPayload` emitted `sortOrder: undefined` and `JSON.stringify` dropped it. **Latent, and
measured to be latent** rather than assumed from the card.

### ⭐ Both conflation hazards excluded — verified independently

| hazard | check | result |
|---|---|---|
| ObjectView's **saved-view** `sortOrder` (mine, found at census) | files touching `ObjectView` in the diff | **0** ✔ |
| the **object-level** `sortOrder` (#6223's, deliberately kept) | still present in `MetadataService.ts` | ✔ |
| `sortable` (triage's named hazard — a boolean, different concept) | untouched, and now **asserted** | ✔ |

⭐ And better than untouched: the new comment at `MetadataService.ts:103-104` names **both**
siblings explicitly — *"Distinct from the object-level `sortOrder` retired by objectui#6223, and
from the saved-view `sortOrder` in `ObjectView.tsx`."* The two traps I flagged at dispatch are now
disarmed **in the code**, for every future reader, rather than surviving as a hazard I happened to
catch this once.

That came from censusing the shape — *a field-metadata payload key `FieldSchema` refuses* — rather
than the identifier, which is exactly what the dispatch asked for and what a bare `sortOrder` grep
would have got wrong three ways.

### The resolution style was chosen by measurement, not inherited by default

The charter allowed "drop it, **or** map it to a real spec concept if one exists." The dev
established that **none exists**: the spec has no field-level ordering key at all and models field
order by **declaration order in the object's `fields` record**. So #4687's delete-with-zero-readers
style applies rather than #6041's rename. ⭐ **Both facts are now asserted rather than left as
prose** — which is what stops the next reader re-litigating whether a mapping was missed.

### ⭐⭐ A removal's evidence, done properly — including three positive controls

A deletion has no new behaviour to pin, so the structural claim is measured: `FieldMetadataPayload`
16 → 15 declared, `DesignerFieldDefinition` 19 → 18, and the ledger line gone.

⭐ And **three positive controls in the same unchanged output** prove it is a removal rather than a
blinded scanner: `enabled objectui#6238` still ledgered, `sortOrder (ObjectDefinition, vs
ObjectSchema)` still `uiOnly`, `referenceTo (DesignerFieldDefinition…)` still `uiOnly`. A
before/after that shows only shrinkage, with siblings proven still visible, is the difference
between "the key is gone" and "the instrument stopped looking".

⚠️ Note the gate-script edit is in the **allowed direction**: the `KNOWN_UNPARSEABLE_KEYS` entry
was **removed**, i.e. the ledger *shrank*. Shrinking a shrink-only list is the supported move;
adding to one is the weakening that sits on the human floor.

### ⭐⭐ The second predicted direction, and why it matters more than the first

> the parity gate stayed **GREEN** on the mutated tree, because the mutation restored only the
> copier and the gate reads **declarations** — so the new runtime pin covers the half the gate's own
> coverage notes say it cannot see, and is not redundant with it.

That is a *proof the new pin adds coverage*, not just a proof it can fail. Most reverse
verifications establish only the latter; predicting and confirming which existing gate stays blind
is what shows the pin is worth its maintenance.

Reverse verification proper: mutation confirmed on disk by grep count **and** blob-hash difference
before any reading; `Tests 2 failed | 4 passed (6)` with `expected true to be false` on
`expect('sortOrder' in def).toBe(false)`; restore proven by hash with `git diff HEAD` empty.

One fixture in `MetadataService.specKeyObjectPayload.test.ts` **pinned exactly the deleted branch**
and was replaced rather than respelled — the honest treatment when the thing a test pinned no
longer exists.

Prerequisite failures reported as prerequisites, not findings: the cold type-check's TS2307 wall
before the closure build, and `check-readme-exports`' 69 "run `pnpm build` first" items, none of
which name `packages/types`, `DesignerFieldDefinition` or `sortOrder`.

### Landing

⛔ Not enqueued — 19 green, **10 still running**, 0 failures, `behind` (⛔ not syncing).
